ACCESS.ANYONE_WITH_THE_URL: Anyone with the URL and your x-blocks-key can call it. No identity, no token-scoped work.
ACCESS.NO_EXTRA_RESTRICTION_ANY: No extra restriction — any signed-in caller with a valid Blocks token can invoke it.
CONNECTIONS.DEPENDENCIES_IN_PACKAGE_JSON: "dependencies" in package.json must be an object.
CONNECTIONS.PACKAGE_JSON_IS_NOT: package.json is not valid JSON — fix it first, then update.
CONNECTIONS.PACKAGE_JSON_IS_NOT_2: package.json is not valid JSON — fix it first, then add the connection.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.ACCESS_KEY_OF_AN: Access key of an IAM user allowed sqs:SendMessage on that queue
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.ANY_MONGODB_WITH_A: Any MongoDB with a public endpoint — Atlas, Cosmos DB for MongoDB.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.ANY_MYSQL_OR_MARIAD: Any MySQL or MariaDB with a public endpoint — PlanetScale, Azure, RDS.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.ANY_POSTGRES_WITH_A: Any Postgres with a public endpoint — Neon, Supabase, Azure, RDS.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.ANY_REDIS_WITH_A: Any Redis with a public TLS endpoint — Upstash, Redis Cloud, Azure Cache.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.DATA_MAIL_IAM_AND: Data, mail, IAM and notifier through @seliseblocks/client, as the signed-in caller — or a client-credentials client when there is none.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.OPTIONAL_AN_IAM_CLI: Optional: an IAM client-credentials client, used only when a run has no caller token (public trigger, scheduled workflow)
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.PUBLISH_TO_ANY_AMQP: Publish to any AMQP broker with a public endpoint — CloudAMQP, Amazon MQ.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.SEND_TO_AN_SQS: Send to an SQS queue with an IAM user's access key.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.SEND_TO_YOUR_OWN: Send to your own Service Bus namespace.
CONNECTIONS_CONSTANT.THE_PROJECT_S_API: The project's API host: https://blocksapi.<your domain>, or the shared public host until the project has a custom domain
FORMAT.HANDLER_RAN_TOO_SHORT: Handler ran {{value}}: too short to compare with the limit
FUNCTIONS_PAGE.DEPLOY_CODE_AND_CALL: Deploy code and call it over HTTP or from a workflow — it runs in an isolated sandbox.
FUNCTIONS_PAGE.THE_REQUEST_FAILED_BEFORE: The request failed before the list came back. Nothing has changed — try again.
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.APPLIED_TO_EVERY_IN: Applied to every invocation, the same for every function.
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.CONNECT_MONGODB_RED: Connect MongoDB, Redis and Blocks APIs
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.EXPORT_DOWNLOADED_U: Export downloaded. Unsaved changes are not in it.
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.FIND_AND_REPLACE_CL: Find and replace — click again to close
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.NATIVE_0_FETCH_0: Native <0>fetch()</0>, async/await and npm packages. Variables arrive as <1>ctx.env.NAME</1> — inside the handler, where <2>ctx</2> exists. Calls reuse the sandbox: open connections at module level, keep request data in the handler, and await everything or use <3>ctx.waitUntil()</3>.
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.RUN_THE_FUNCTION_WI: Run the function with a sample request
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.VERSION_RANGES_INST: version ranges · installed on Test and Deploy
FUNCTION_DETAIL_PAGE.WHAT_HAPPENS_WHEN_A: What happens when a run fails.
FUNCTION_TYPES.FINISH_WORK_AFTER_THE: Finish work after the answer is sent, without making the reused sandbox be replaced.
FUNCTION_TYPES.GETACCESSTOKEN_THE_CALLER: getAccessToken() — the caller's Blocks token, fetched on demand (await it), or undefined.
FUNCTION_TYPES.INFO_WARN_ERROR_DEBUG: info / warn / error / debug — kept on the run.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.AWAIT_A_DELAY_INSIDE: Await a delay inside the handler, or clear the timer before you return. For repeating work, use a scheduled workflow with a Function step.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.AWAIT_IT_IF_IT: Await it. If it may finish after the answer, pass it to ctx.waitUntil.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.CAPPED_PER_RUN_LINES: Capped per run; lines past the cap are dropped
LIMITS_CONSTANT.CONNECT_AND_CLOSE_A: Connect and close a database client on every call.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.CREATE_THE_CLIENT_ONCE: Create the client once at module level and reuse it. Don't close it per call.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.FINISH_WORK_AFTER_THE: Finish work after the answer is sent, within the time limit — in every mode (reused sandbox, Test run, workflow step).
LIMITS_CONSTANT.ID_VERSION_ATTEMPT_AND: id, version, attempt, and invokedBy { type, id } — type is http, workflow, test or replay.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.KEEP_CTX_CTX_LOG: Keep ctx, ctx.log or a token from ctx.blocks.getAccessToken() for later — for example in a client's event listener or a module-level variable.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.KEEP_PER_CALL_DATA: Keep per-call data in local variables. Module level is for clients, constants and caches keyed by tenant.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.LEAVE_A_SETTIMEOUT_OR: Leave a setTimeout or setInterval running after the handler returns.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.READ_CTX_ONLY_INSIDE: Read ctx only inside the handler. In listeners that outlive the call, use console.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.SIZE_LIMITED_A_LARGER: Size-limited; a larger request is refused
LIMITS_CONSTANT.SIZE_LIMITED_RETURN_A: Size-limited; return a reference for large data
LIMITS_CONSTANT.SMALL_TMP_ONLY_FILES: Small /tmp only; files can't be executed
LIMITS_CONSTANT.STANDARD_FETCH_PUBLIC_IN: Standard fetch. Public internet is reachable; Blocks internals and private networks are not routed.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.START_WORK_AND_RETURN: Start work and return without waiting for it.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.STORE_REQUEST_DATA_IN: Store request data in module-level variables — the next caller can see it.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.STRUCTURED_LINES_KEPT_ON: Structured lines kept on the run. console.log is captured too.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.TENANTID_USERID_ROLES_PE: tenantId, userId, roles, permissions, isAuthenticated. Empty identity on a public call — never a privileged token.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.THE_CALLER_S_BLOCKS: The caller's Blocks token: pass it as accessToken to @seliseblocks/client, with ctx.context.tenantId as xBlocksKey. In a warm sandbox it is fetched only when you ask (one IAM round trip, once per call), so ask only on the path that calls Blocks. undefined when there is no signed-in caller (a public trigger, a scheduled workflow) or for a client-credentials caller — check it before calling Blocks. Masked in logs. ctx.blocks.accessToken was removed.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.THE_REQUEST_METHOD_PATH: The request: { method, path, query, headers, body }. path is whatever followed /fn/{id}; body is the parsed JSON (or text) of a POST, null on a GET. From a workflow node it is the previous node's output instead.
LIMITS_CONSTANT.YOUR_VARIABLES_AS_PLAIN: Your variables, as plain strings. Snapshotted at deploy. A variable bound to a secret arrives as its real value, masked in logs.
REUSE_HINTS.CTX_BLOCKS_ACCESSTOKEN_WAS_R: ctx.blocks.accessToken was removed. Use `await ctx.blocks.getAccessToken()` — the caller's token is now fetched only when your code asks for it.
REUSE_HINTS.KEEPS_THIS_CALL_S: Keeps this call's data in a module-level variable. The next call — maybe another user's — runs in the same sandbox and sees it. Use a variable inside the handler.
REUSE_HINTS.SETINTERVAL_KEEPS_RUNNING_AF: setInterval keeps running after the call ends, so the sandbox is replaced after it. Clear it before returning. For repeating work, use a scheduled workflow with a Function step.
REUSE_HINTS.THIS_FETCH_IS_NOT: This fetch is not awaited. If the call answers first, the request is cut off and the sandbox is replaced. Use await, return it, or ctx.waitUntil(fetch(…)).
REUSE_HINTS.THIS_LISTENER_OUTLIVES_THE: This listener outlives the call but uses ctx. Later events would run with an old call's ctx. Use console inside listeners.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.A_VARIABLE_IS_BOUND: A variable is bound to a secret that could not be read — it was deleted, locked, has no value, or is not readable by this run. Nothing ran. Rebind the variable named above to an existing secret, then run again.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.HANDLER_SCOPE: input and ctx are parameters of your handler — they exist only inside export default async function handler(input, ctx) { … }, not at the top level of the file. Code outside the handler runs once when the sandbox starts, which is where clients, caches and constants belong; anything that needs the request or the context has to be inside.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.MISSING_PACKAGE: The import could not be resolved. Add the package to package.json — pinned to an exact version — then run the test again, which builds a new image.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.MODULE_THREW: The file threw while it was being imported, so the handler never ran and nothing was logged. The cause is in top-level code, not inside your handler.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.NO_RUNNER_EVER_PICKED: No runner ever picked this up, so nothing ran. It is safe to run again — but check the runners are healthy first, because the platform already gave up on delivering it once.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_FUNCTION_RETURNED: The function returned successfully, but an output action did not deliver.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_FUNCTION_STARTED_: The function started more processes or threads than a sandbox allows.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_FUNCTION_USED_MOR: The function used more memory than its limit. Hold less in memory.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_HANDLER_THREW_THE: The handler threw. The stack is in the logs below.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_IMAGE_COULD_NOT: The image could not be pulled — it is no longer on the registry. The build behind it has been invalidated, so testing or deploying again builds a new one.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_RETURNED_VALUE_CO: The returned value could not be turned into JSON. Return plain objects, arrays and primitives.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_RETURNED_VALUE_IS: The returned value is over the result size limit. Return a reference instead of the payload.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_RUN_COULD_NOT: The run could not be queued, so nothing ran. The platform's queue was unavailable for a moment — running it again is safe.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_RUN_NEVER_REPORTE: The run never reported back and the platform closed it. It may or may not have finished its work, so check for side effects before running it again.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_RUN_PASSED_ITS: The run passed its timeout and was stopped. Do less work per call.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_SANDBOX_COULD_NOT: The sandbox could not start the runtime — usually a broken package.json or a package that needs a native build.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_SANDBOX_FAILED_TO: The sandbox failed to start. Nothing ran, so a replay is safe.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_SECRET_STORE_COUL: The secret store could not be reached while the run was starting, so nothing ran. This is on the platform's side. An HTTP run of a deployed function may be retried automatically; running it again is safe.
RUN_ERROR_CONSTANT.THE_TEST_S_IMAGE: The test's image could not be built, so nothing ran. The build log above says why — usually a package name or version in package.json that does not exist.
TEMPLATES.AN_EMPTY_HANDLER_THAT: An empty handler that logs its input and returns it.
TEMPLATES.CALLS_AN_HTTP_API: Calls an HTTP API with fetch(), reshapes the response and returns it.
TEMPLATES.CONNECTS_TO_MONGODB_ONCE: Connects to MongoDB once at module level and reuses it on every call — the fast pattern.
TEMPLATES.ECHOES_THE_REQUEST_BACK: Echoes the request back with the caller's identity from ctx.context.
TRANSFER.ONLY_JSON_EXPORT_FILES: Only .json export files can be imported.
TRANSFER.SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH: This export uses schema version {{found}}, but this environment reads version {{expected}}. Export the function again and import the new file.
TRANSFER.THE_REQUEST_COULD_NOT: The request could not be completed.
TRANSFER.THIS_FILE_IS_LARGER: This file is larger than 3 MB, so it cannot be a function export.
TRANSFER.THIS_FILE_IS_NOT_VALID_JSON: This file is not valid JSON.
TRANSFER.THIS_IS_A_PROXY_EXPORT: This is a proxy export, not a function export.
TRANSFER.THIS_IS_NOT_A_FUNCTION_EXPORT: This is not a function export file.
TRIGGER.AWAIT_EVERY_CALL_OR: Await every call, or use ctx.waitUntil() for work that should finish after the answer.
TRIGGER.A_NEWER_VERSION_WENT: A newer version went live, so this version's sandbox was retired after the call.
TRIGGER.CODE_LEFT_RUNNING_BY: Code left running by an earlier call ran during this call.
TRIGGER.THE_CALL_OR_WORK: The call, or work passed to ctx.waitUntil(), ran past its time limit, so the sandbox was stopped.
TRIGGER.THE_FUNCTION_LEFT_RUNNING: The function left {{what}} running after it answered.
TRIGGER.THE_SANDBOX_CRASHED_DURING: The sandbox crashed during the call.
TRIGGER.THE_SANDBOX_REACHED_ITS: The sandbox reached its call limit and was replaced with a fresh one.
TRIGGER.THE_SANDBOX_REACHED_ITS_2: The sandbox reached its age limit and was replaced with a fresh one.
TRIGGER.THE_SANDBOX_SENT_SOMETHING: The sandbox sent something unexpected, so it was replaced.
TRIGGER.THE_SANDBOX_S_MEMORY: The sandbox's memory was close to its limit, so it was replaced with a fresh one.
TRIGGER.WAITUNTIL_WORK_UNFINISHED: ctx.waitUntil() work that did not finish in time
USE_RUN_STREAM.THE_STREAM_ENDED_WITH: The stream ended with an error.
